title: The promise at the other end
subtitle: A customer story for the Frontier era
label: Independent customer-facing concept
description: An illustrative customer story connecting AI and agents with human judgment, customer trust and business outcomes. Created for this portfolio.

slides.title: The promise at the other end
slides.text: Begin with the person at the other end of a business process. A store opening is a date on a project plan, but it is also the first shift for a new employee, the first visit from a neighbor, and a promise a customer expects someone to keep. This fictional story explores how Microsoft Frontier Company’s approach could help a retailer give its people more capacity to deliver. This is an independent portfolio concept, not official Microsoft material.

links.name: Microsoft Frontier Company
links.detail: Current approach, embedded expertise, production deployment, intelligence and trust.

slides.title: We open on Friday. Will we be ready?
slides.text: Imagine Maya, a regional operations leader for a growing retailer. The newest store opens on Friday. A critical refrigeration delivery has slipped. The store team is ready. The neighborhood is waiting. Maya hears a simple question, and she wants to answer it honestly. Pause after the question. Ask the customer to think of the equivalent promise inside their own organization.

slides.title: The answer is scattered across the business
slides.text: The business already has much of what Maya needs. Inventory knows where a replacement unit sits. Procurement has the latest supplier update. The store team knows when the installation crew is available. Finance owns the exception policy. The burden of assembling that picture falls on Maya. While she searches and reconciles, the team waits to decide. This is the workflow we want to improve.

slides.title: What if the next step arrived with the answer?
slides.text: Now change the experience. Maya still owns the outcome. But instead of opening one more tab, she receives a connected view of the situation, the evidence behind it, and a proposed next step. AI can help retrieve and interpret information. Connected agents and workflows can help prepare and carry out approved actions. The business question is where that combination changes the customer experience.

slides.title: The Frontier opportunity starts inside your business
slides.text: Microsoft Frontier Company brings industry expertise and AI engineering into customer organizations to connect AI with business workflows and measurable outcomes. The distinctive asset is the customer’s own knowledge: its data, experience and decision processes. The design also needs trust: identity, access, oversight and an operating model. Together, those make the workflow useful in the context of this customer’s business.

slides.title: Maya gets a shared picture, with the gaps visible
slides.text: In the proposed workflow, an agent checks approved sources and assembles the situation. It identifies the delayed unit, a possible alternative and the installation constraint. Crucially, it shows what it cannot yet verify: the carrier has not confirmed a replacement delivery. A useful system makes the gap visible. It does not turn an inference into a customer commitment. Sources and timestamps should travel with the recommendation.

slides.title: The next step becomes a recovery plan
slides.text: The system proposes a recovery plan against the retailer’s rules. Check the alternative unit’s suitability, request the transfer and transport options, prepare the cost exception and draft an update for the store manager. Each step has an owner. The recommendation includes dependencies and unanswered questions. It is an example of connected work, not an out-of-the-box product demonstration or a promise that AI can fix every delay.

slides.title: The choice still belongs to Maya
slides.text: The system prepares. Maya decides. She reviews the evidence, weighs customer impact and approves the appropriate spend. A designated owner confirms any new customer promise. We deliberately keep these decisions in human hands in this scenario. If information conflicts, permissions fail or the agent cannot verify an action, the workflow stops and escalates to a person. Accountability must be designed, tested and operated.

slides.title: The work keeps moving after the decision
slides.text: Once the decision is approved, configured workflows can update systems, assign tasks and monitor progress. The loop closes only when the business verifies what actually happened. Did the replacement arrive? Did the store open as promised? Where did the workflow fail? The team uses those observations to improve the process, the data and the agent. That continuous improvement is central to the Frontier Company approach.

slides.title: The technology follows the work
slides.text: This is an illustrative solution pattern, not a prescribed architecture. Maya could interact with an agent in her familiar Microsoft 365 environment. Copilot Studio can connect agents and workflows to approved enterprise systems. Microsoft governance capabilities support identity, access, data policy and visibility. The actual pattern depends on the customer’s landscape, requirements, licensing and controls. The customer experience and business outcome decide what needs to be built.

slides.title: Success is visible in the customer experience
slides.text: Before rollout, agree on a baseline and define the business result with the customer. We can measure how long exceptions take to resolve, whether commitments hold, whether customers must contact us again and the full cost of handling the exception. Include AI and operating costs. Compare comparable cases and watch quality and safety together. This slide proposes measures. It does not claim that this scenario has produced results.

slides.title: One production workflow creates a path to scale
slides.text: Start with a real operational workflow and an accountable business owner. Define the result, the boundary of delegation and the failure conditions. Validate against realistic cases, including missing and conflicting data. Roll out through explicit operational gates with monitoring and fallback. Then expand only where the evidence justifies it. This is a proposed adoption path, not an official Microsoft delivery schedule. The intention is production value with a design that can extend.

slides.title: Which customer promise will we protect first?
slides.text: Return to the person at the other end. When the workflow works, the customer feels a clear answer, a reliable commitment and a business that follows through. Maya gains room to apply her judgment where it matters. End with a concrete invitation: choose one customer promise, the workflow behind it and the leader accountable for improving it. That is the starting point for the conversation. This is an independent concept created for Meghan Fasano’s portfolio, not official Microsoft material.
